title: Barbecue across the country and Jackson's love of food
summary: Chicago barbecue was best, with Magnus Clark in Detroit and an Evansville pit; Jackson says food was his vice instead of drink.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I was trying to think of the name of that restaurant in Cleveland that we used to go to across the Majestic Hotel.
Oh, yeah, and they got up the street -- they had the barbecue place across the street.
The best barbecue you will ever --
Well, you know, you can get good barbecue, but to me, of the middle western states there was no barbecue like Chicago. You could get some barbecue in Chicago.
The only place that come close to Chicago barbecue was a place in Detroit, a guy called Magnus.
He had wonderful barbecue. And there used to be a place in Evansville, too, Evansville, Indiana, --
-- where the guy used to cook it in the pit. He used to go right in there and take if right off the pit.
You know, originally Evansville, Indiana, was Big Sid Catlett's home originally --
-- before he came to Chicago. We used to -- I saw his father there and a lot of his people. But -- Louisville was another good place.
Oh, yeah. Louisville. There were a lot of nice places to eat there.
I don't know how we got off on this food thing, but we were talking about piano players. Maybe pianos and food and you and I and food because we always enjoyed it.
Me, yes. You know, I love my food. That was my biggest -- I never was a real drinker -- I smoked a little bit -- but food was always my thing.
The guys would be going out hunting to drink, I would hunt something to eat.
